text: 64 teams in a knockout cup: five rounds and a final. Rounds 1 and 2: two pots, one with the Bundesliga and 2. text: Final table in 2026-27, as the FIGC's Federal Council decided on 26 May 2026 on the proposal of the Lega Calcio Serie A, departing for this season from art. 51 of the NOIF. If two teams finish level on points in first place, the title (Campione d'Italia) goes to the winner of a single play-off match at the home of the team better placed in the mini-table (classifica avulsa); if it is level after normal time, there is no extra time and penalties decide. Where more than two teams are level, and for all the other places in the table, the classifica avulsa decides in this order: a) points in the matches between the teams concerned, b) goal difference in those matches, c) goal difference over the whole championship, d) goals scored over the whole championship, e) drawing of lots. If a team that would play the play-off is a finalist in a UEFA competition, the classifica avulsa decides instead. The number of clubs, matches per club and points per win are not stated on any page of the organiser or the federation that could be read (see the Wikipedia row).

If more than two teams are level, the classifica avulsa picks the two; if one of them is a finalist in a UEFA competition, the classifica avulsa decides instead. The Regionalliga Nordost champion goes up directly this season (the direct place rotates between Nord, Nordost and Bayern), and the West and Südwest champions every season. The matches are DFB matches under DFB rules; the DFB supervises and organises the round.
basis: published: BFV Auf- und Abstiegsregelung der Regionalliga Bayern for 2026/2027 and the NOFV's Regionalliga Nordost page naming 2026/27 (two organisers, each for the season), with the BFV's league page (2026/27) and the NFV's league page (no season) for the rotation and the DFB's role. Read in runs 2 and 3 of PR #234.

text: 2026-27: late May to early June 2027. The matches follow the Regionalliga Bayern's last matchday, which its framework calendar puts in late May 2027; in 2026 the first leg was at the end of May and the return at the start of June. Month level only; the days will be on the organiser's pages.
basis: Inferred from the BFV framework calendar 2026/2027 for the Regionalliga Bayern (Stand June 2026, read in run 3 of PR #234) and the 2026 dates in Wikipedia (de) Fußball-Regionalliga 2025/26 (run 4; observed past cycle, one third-party source).

text: The DFB supervises and organises the round, so it fixes the days and kick-offs; its sites are closed to this research. In 2026 the matches came at the end of May and the start of June, after the Regionalliga seasons ended. Expect the same pattern in 2027 and check the dates by hand.
basis: Inferred (CLAUDE.md rule 9: schedule rows are month level and inferred only; observed past cycle): the DFB's role from the NFV's league page (run 3 of PR #234) and the 2026 dates from Wikipedia (de) Fußball-Regionalliga 2025/26 (run 4). One cycle.

text: The DFB, which runs the round, has its sites closed to this research, so follow the two leagues whose champions meet in 2027. Bayern (BFV): the Regionalliga Bayern page and its results page (which showed the 2025-26 season when read), the BFV app (results, news, push messages for favourite leagues and teams), the monthly BFV fan newsletter, and the BFV's TV and video page (BFV.TV, Sporttotal.tv livestreams); the BFV's league page links a WhatsApp channel and a YouTube channel (listed, not opened). Nord (NFV): the Regionalliga Nord page, its results service (it loads fussball.de only after a consent click, not made), the newsletter sign-up, and the links NordFV Live (nordfv.tv), Facebook, Instagram and YouTube (listed, not opened). No page read names a broadcaster for the 2027 matches.
basis: The organisers of the two feeding leagues, not of the round; their pages show no season except the BFV's league page (2026/27) and results page (2025/26). Read in runs 3 and 4 of PR #234.

text: Holder: in 2026 Würzburger Kickers, from the Regionalliga Bayern, beat 1. FC Lokomotive Leipzig, champion of the Regionalliga Nordost, and play in the 3. Liga in 2026-27; the Bavarian champion, 1. FC Nürnberg II, had waived its place in the matches. The best-placed team entitled to promotion takes part; had a team waived or a league had none, the other side would have had a bye.
basis: published: the BFV's Regionalliga Bayern page (showing 2026/27) and Wikipedia (de) Fußball-Regionalliga 2025/26, two independent sources, read in runs 3 and 4 of PR #234; the bye rule is Wikipedia only. The scores are in the format row.

text: Knockout cup, one match per tie: level after 90 minutes, 2 x 15 minutes of extra time, then penalties; five substitutions. Round 1 is drawn in three regions (Odenwald, Rhein-Neckar, Mittelbaden), round 2 from a seeding list; in both the lower-tier club is at home as a rule. From round 3 (32 teams) the draw covers the whole association, again with a seeding list; the lower-tier club keeps home right in rounds 3 and 4, and 3. Liga and Regionalliga clubs cannot meet before the quarter-final. The quarter- and semi-finals are drawn separately: Kreisliga and Kreisklasse clubs are at home against the higher leagues, and the regulation also swaps home right there when two association clubs at least one amateur level apart meet. For the final the bfv may set its own terms.
basis: published: the bfv's Durchführungsbestimmungen for the 2026/27 men's cup (dated 14 September 2026).

text: The winner gets the association's place in the first round of the next season's DFB-Pokal: SV Waldhof Mannheim, winner of 2025-26, plays in round 1 of the 2026-27 DFB-Pokal. The winner pays 25 % of the DFB's marketing money for that round (plus VAT) into a solidarity pot that the bfv shares out among the cup's participants; it keeps its other DFB-Pokal income. If the cup cannot be finished before the DFB's entry deadline, the bfv board names the entrant on the proposal of the competitions committee.
basis: published: the bfv's Durchführungsbestimmungen 2026/27 (dated 14 September 2026) and its news of the 2025-26 final (May 2026).

text: 2026-27, month level: round 1 in July 2026 (after a June draw), round 2 the following weekend, round 3 with the 3. Liga and Regionalliga clubs in early August and the round of 16 in August 2026; from the quarter-final on, dates are agreed with the clubs, and the bfv's October 2026 news put the quarter-finals in the second half of October. The final is part of the Finaltag der Amateure, which the bfv's framework calendar puts on the day of the DFB-Pokal final in May 2027.
basis: published: the bfv's news of 1 July 2026 and 15 October 2026 and its framework calendar 2026/27 (Stand 7 January 2026); the day-level dates stay on those pages.

text: In 2026 the bfv drew the first rounds at the end of June, streamed the draw on Instagram, and published standard dates for rounds 1 to 3 and the round of 16 in its draw news; the quarter- and semi-finals are drawn separately and their dates agreed with the clubs.
basis: Inferred (CLAUDE.md rule 9: schedule rows are month level and inferred only; observed past cycle): one cycle, from the bfv's men's page, its news of 1 July 2026 and its Durchführungsbestimmungen 2026/27.

text: The organiser's channels: the bfv's men's page (cup news, the 2026/27 regulation and framework calendar) and the bfv news. Results: the men's page links the cup's fussball.de page (not opened: fussball.de is closed to this research), and the home club runs the fussball.de live ticker. Live: in 2026-27 the six quarter- and semi-finals stream live with commentary on LEAGUES (leagues.football/bfv-pokal), which sells one pass for the whole cup season, with replays, and marks the matches it shows. Draws: the first-round draw was streamed on Instagram. The final: on the Finaltag der Amateure, when Das Erste showed the 21 men's finals in 2026. Newsletter: by e-mail request to the bfv press office. Social: the bfv's Facebook and Instagram accounts (listed, not opened).
basis: published: the bfv's men's page, regulation 2026/27 (dated 14 September 2026) and news of 15 October 2026; the LEAGUES cup page (no season shown); the bfv's newsletter page (no season shown).

text: Identity and entry: the men's cup of the Badischer Fußballverband (bfv), which runs it; called Volksbanken Raiffeisenbanken bfv-Pokal since 2026-27 (bfv-Rothaus-Pokal in 2025-26). 116 teams in 2026-27: 1 from the 3. Liga, 3 Regionalliga, 3 Oberliga, 11 Verbandsliga, 48 Landesliga, 40 Kreisliga, 9 Kreisklasse A and 1 Kreisklasse B; the nine districts send fixed quotas (Karlsruhe 8; Heidelberg, Mannheim and Pforzheim 6 each; the other five 4 each). Second teams, and joint teams that include one, may not enter. Taking part is compulsory up to the round of 16 and voluntary from the quarter-final, which needs a signed participation agreement. The holder and the Regionalliga clubs enter in round 3.
basis: published: the bfv's Durchführungsbestimmungen 2026/27 (dated 14 September 2026), its news of 1 July 2026 and of the 2025-26 final.

text: Holder on the checked date: SV Waldhof Mannheim (3. Liga), winner of 2025-26: 3:0 against VfR Mannheim in the final on the Finaltag der Amateure in May 2026 at the Carl-Benz-Stadion in Mannheim, before 16,951 spectators; its first cup win since 2022.
basis: published: the bfv's news of the 2025-26 final (May 2026); the bfv's news of 1 July 2026 calls Waldhof the title holder.

text: Tickets for a tie: the home club handles tickets, the ticket booths and the taking of entry money (the visiting club may send its own people), and sends the visiting team five guest tickets for its officials; the players and staff of the visiting team enter without a ticket. Up to the semi-final the association takes 10 % of the net takings and the club whose ground is used gets 20 % for its costs; for the final the bfv may set different terms. No sale dates are given.
basis: published: the bfv's Durchführungsbestimmungen 2026/27 (dated 14 September 2026).

text: 64 teams in a knockout cup; the final is played on the Finaltag der Amateure. The draw, the home right and the extra-time rule were not found: the SBFV's Spielordnung (§ 50) leaves the cup's details to an Ausführungsbestimmung (AB 2), which was not read.
basis: published: the SBFV's men's page (naming the season 2026/2027) and its Spielordnung (Stand August 2026).

basis: published: the SBFV's men's page (naming the season 2026/2027) and its Spielordnung (Stand August 2026).

text: 2026-27, month level: the final is on the Finaltag der Amateure in May 2027, the day of the DFB-Pokal final, as the SBFV's framework calendar shows. The other rounds were not read: the cup columns of the calendar did not survive the PDF conversion clearly.

basis: published: the SBFV's Finaltag page (naming the 2026 edition), its men's page (naming 2026/2027) and its media page (no season shown).

text: Identity and entry: the men's cup of the Südbadischer Fußballverband (SBFV), called Volksbanken Raiffeisenbanken SBFV-Pokal since 2026-27. Entry is compulsory for the association's clubs in the Regionalliga, Oberliga, Verbandsliga and Landesliga and for the district cups' semi-finalists; a club may not enter a second team. Cup matches are compulsory fixtures under the Spielordnung. The 2025-26 winner, and so the holder, is not named on any page read: left blank.
basis: published: the SBFV's men's page (naming the season 2026/2027) and its Spielordnung (Stand August 2026).

text: Tickets and takings: the Spielordnung's rule for cup and decider matches has the body running the match set the entry prices, with no discount for the clubs' members. On a neutral ground the host club keeps 20 % of the gross after VAT and the two teams share the rest equally; on one club's ground the takings after VAT are split in half and each side bears its own costs. No sale dates are given.
basis: published: the SBFV's Spielordnung (Stand August 2026), § 51a.

text: Knockout cup, one match per tie; every round is drawn. The lower-tier club is at home, and with clubs of the same level the one drawn first; the two may agree to swap. Level after normal time at association level: 2 x 15 minutes of extra time, then penalties; up to five substitutions. The teams are split into four geographic groups up to the round of 16, which is drawn across the whole association. The final is in principle on a neutral ground.
basis: published: the WFV's Durchführungsbestimmungen for the 2026/2027 men's cup (Stand September 2026) and its news of 19 August 2026.

text: The winner goes straight into the first round of the DFB-Pokal. The district cup winners of a season enter the next season's WFV-Pokal at association level (if a district winner is promoted to the Landesliga, its beaten finalist enters too).
basis: published: the WFV's cup page and its Durchführungsbestimmungen 2026/2027 (Stand September 2026).

basis: published: the WFV's news of 19 August 2026, its list of finals and its men's framework calendar 2026/27; the day-level dates stay on those pages.

basis: Inferred (CLAUDE.md rule 9: schedule rows are month level and inferred only; observed past cycle): one draw, from the WFV's news of 19 August 2026.

text: Identity and entry: the men's cup of the Württembergischer Fußballverband (WFV), run at association level by its competitions committee and at district level by the districts; called Volksbanken Raiffeisenbanken WFV-Pokal since 2026. Taking part is compulsory. At association level at most 128 teams: the WFV's teams in the 3. Liga, the Regionalliga Südwest and the Oberliga Baden-Württemberg, the Verbandsliga and Landesliga teams and the previous season's district cup winners; from the quarter-final a participation agreement is needed. The 2026-27 field has 108 teams in four groups (26, 28, 27 and 27); the 3. Liga club and the four Regionalliga clubs had a bye in round 1. Whether reserve teams may enter was not found in the documents read.
basis: published: the WFV's Durchführungsbestimmungen 2026/2027 (Stand September 2026), its 2026/27 field and its cup page.

text: Holder and history: SG Sonnenhof Großaspach, winner of 2025-26: 4:1 against SV Stuttgarter Kickers in the final in May 2026 at the GAZi-Stadion auf der Waldau in Stuttgart, before 8,533 spectators; it also won 2024-25 (2:0 against TSG Balingen at the same ground) and the WFV counts three titles in all. The WFV lists finals since 1950-51; there was no competition in 1951-52 and 1952-53.
basis: published: the WFV's list of finals and its news of 19 August 2026, which calls Großaspach the holder.

text: Tickets: at association level the usual local entry prices apply; the clubs' members pay the full price, honorary and free tickets are not allowed, and the visiting club may send its own people to check the ticket sales. For the final the competitions committee may set different accounting terms. No sale dates are given.
basis: published: the WFV's Durchführungsbestimmungen 2026/2027 (Stand September 2026), sections 8 and 9.

text: Knockout cup, one match per tie. The lower-tier club is at home, and with clubs of the same level the one drawn first. A tie level after normal time goes straight to penalties, with no extra time; the winner must play the next round. The final, and the district finals, may be at a participating club's ground or on a neutral ground. Toto-Pokal dates in the framework calendar take precedence over league matches and may fall on weekdays. 64 teams play the first BFV main round, among them the 22 district winners.
basis: published: the BFV's Spielordnung (Stand 6 July 2026), §§ 68 and 69; the BFV's Toto-Pokal page (no season label) for the 64 teams.

In 2026 the winner, Würzburger Kickers, had already qualified as Bavarian amateur champion, and the BFV wrote that the beaten finalist TSV 1860 München could plan for the DFB-Pokal as well. The BFV puts the guaranteed DFB-Pokal money at about 210,000 euros; LOTTO Bayern paid the 2026 winner 7,600 euros.
basis: published: the BFV's Spielordnung (Stand 6 July 2026), § 68 no. 8; its news of the 2026 final (May 2026) and of the 2026-27 semi-final draw (October 2026).

FC Schweinfurt 05 against FC Ingolstadt 04, the Regionalliga club at home in both.

text: Identity and entry: the men's cup of the Bayerischer Fußball-Verband (BFV), called Toto-Pokal after its long-time partner LOTTO Bayern and played since 1998; the BFV's match committee runs it up to state level and the district committees run the district rounds. Only a member club's first men's team may enter (or a joint team led by one); second and further teams may not. The 3. Liga and Regionalliga Bayern clubs must take part. Bayernliga and Landesliga clubs do not enter the first main round automatically: they qualify during the current league season for the next season's first main round, by matches or table positions set in the BFV's rules for each season. For all other teams the district cup is voluntary.
basis: published: the BFV's Spielordnung (Stand 6 July 2026), § 68, and its news of October 2026; the Toto-Pokal page (no season label) for 1998.

text: Holder and history: FC Würzburger Kickers (Regionalliga Bayern), winner of 2025-26: in the final on the Finaltag der Amateure in May 2026 at its own ground, the Stadion am Dallenberg (11,017 spectators, sold out), it drew 1:1 with TSV 1860 München (3. Liga) and won 5:3 on penalties: its fourth title after 2014, 2016 and 2019. FV Illertissen won in 2025. In the 2026-27 quarter-final TSV Aubstadt knocked out the holder.
basis: published: the BFV's news of the 2026 final (May 2026) and of the 2026-27 semi-final draw (October 2026); the Toto-Pokal page (no season label) for 2025.

text: Knockout cup, one match per tie, drawn in public after an announcement. The team drawn first is at home, except that up to the semi-final the lower-tier team is at home; the home club also stages the match, and a swap needs the match office's consent. To reach a round size such as 32 or 64, round 1 may be a qualifying round with byes for the highest-placed teams. Level after 2 x 15 minutes of extra time: penalties. Up to 16 players may be used.
basis: published: the Berliner FV's Spielordnung (Stand 1 July 2026), § 21.

text: The winner must play in the DFB-Pokal with its first team; if it has already qualified through its league, the beaten finalist is entered instead. Of the share the DFB sets for the association, the losing finalist gets 40 %, the losing semi-finalists 20 % each and the losing quarter-finalists 5 % each. The 2026 final was for the trophy and a place in round 1 of the DFB-Pokal.
basis: published: the Berliner FV's Spielordnung (Stand 1 July 2026), § 21, and its Finaltag der Amateure 2026 page.

text: Knockout cup for Lower Saxony's clubs in the 3. Liga and the Regionalliga Nord, one match per tie, no second leg; in 2026-27 three rounds: quarter-finals, semi-finals and the final (the cup page also names a qualifying round with byes). Every round is drawn, as a rule in public, with byes to fill the first round. The lower-tier club is at home whatever the draw order, otherwise the club drawn first; a home club may cede home right, and one without a floodlit ground loses it. Level after 90 minutes: 2 x 15 minutes of extra time, then penalties. At most five substitutes. Both NFV finals are as a rule at the August-Wenzel-Stadion in Barsinghausen; the NFV may choose another venue, also a finalist's ground.
